terms.gloss: bring oneself to, make up one’s mind to
evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 53 (Lewis & Short s.v. ut)
terms.comment: Literally “to lead one’s mind (to it)”. “I can’t bring myself to …” is nōn possum animum indūcere ut ….

phrases.latin: pater potuit animum indūcere ut nātūram ipsam vinceret
phrases.english: the father could bring himself to overcome nature itself

sources: Lewis & Short: induco · Lewis & Short: animus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 94.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
